summary: The skills are well structured, treat pasted input as data, and stop for approval at the right points, but several of them contradict each other on who may close G0.2 and Decision rows, and three skills write raw pastes into shared files before checking them for row data. The production guard hook has bypasses, some referenced files and paths don't resolve from where an agent runs, and a few outputs (project.json fields, the stale-approval rollup, readiness scans, the rollback decision time) are too loosely defined for different models to produce the same safe result.

findings.claim: The parse flow saves the paste unchanged into upgrade/results/ first, and checks it for row data or query text only afterward (line 50). If a DBA pastes output containing regulated rows, it is already in the Project's shared files, which sync to every machine, before the skill stops. Catch-up and the runbook skill do the same with pasted results and timing sheets.
findings.evidence: precheck SKILL.md L24: "Save the input to `upgrade/results/` unchanged, with one file per database or output." L50: "Don't copy row data or query text into the report. If the paste contains any, stop and ask for a clean rerun." catch-up SKILL.md L15: "Save it to `upgrade/results/`". runbook SKILL.md L30: "Save the sheet unchanged". workspace-layout.mdc L25: "Never put row data, query text or secrets in `upgrade/`." guardrails.mdc L13: "Don't put row data... into prompts, files".
findings.suggested_fix: Make the row-data and query-text screen the first step in all three skills, and save to upgrade/results/ only after it passes. If it fails, discard the paste, save nothing, and ask for a clean rerun.

findings.claim: The precheck skill lets the agent set gate G0.2 to Done itself. Gate review, catch-up and tracker all say an agent never closes a gate. It is also unclear what "every part-1 check passed" means, because some part-1 checks have no pass or fail outcome, only "mark partial" or "record the gap".
findings.evidence: precheck L38: "Set G0.2 to `Done` only if every part-1 check passed". gate-review L31: "Never set a gate to `Done` yourself." catch-up L20: "Gates stay open until `pg-upgrade-gate-review` runs." tracker L55: "Don't mark anything `Done` without evidence, or close gates." reading guide L15: "Mark 4c as partial." L16: "Record the gap."
findings.suggested_fix: Have the precheck skill set G0.2 to Needs approval with the result files as Evidence, and leave closing it to pg-upgrade-gate-review. Define pass or fail for each part-1 check, including whether a partial 4c or a minor-version gap counts as a fail.

findings.claim: Catch-up marks a Decision row Done just because the handoff names the decider. That is a statement, which the same step says is not evidence, and it breaks the tracker checker's rule that Done needs Evidence. An agent told to "fix any errors" may then fill in weak evidence or change the row in some other way.
findings.evidence: catch-up L16: "its status is `Done` only if the handoff names the decider." L17: "Record it ... as \"reported by X on date\", not as evidence." tracker-lib.mjs L81: "Done without Evidence; set it to Needs approval until evidence is linked". evidence-and-sources.mdc rule 4: "A tracker row moves to `Done` only with an `Evidence` link".
findings.suggested_fix: Set handoff decisions to Needs approval, with the named decider as Approver. Mark them Done only when a linked signed record (for example the decision record) is present as Evidence.

findings.claim: Gate review accepts any feeding row that is Waived with an Approver name and a reason. Nothing requires proof that the named person actually approved, so anyone in chat can name an approver and a gate can pass on their say-so. The skill's own rule says that must not happen.
findings.evidence: gate-review L16: "It's `Done` with `Evidence`, or `Waived` with an `Approver` and a reason." L45: "Don't pass a gate on someone's say-so in chat." tracker L15: "To set `Waived`, it needs a named `Approver` and a reason in `Notes`."
findings.suggested_fix: Require a waiver to link evidence of approval, such as a PR approval, a signed decision record entry or a message link from the named approver, and fail the check without it.

findings.claim: The guard hook only blocks a Postgres client when a remote host is written out on the command line, and it treats any host starting with "/" as local. So psql through a Cloud SQL Auth Proxy Unix socket (/cloudsql/...), `psql "$DATABASE_URL"`, `psql service=prod`, or an earlier `export PGHOST=...` in a separate command all get through. guardrails.mdc tells agents the hook blocks these commands.
findings.evidence: L91: `return LOCAL_HOSTS.has(host.toLowerCase()) || host.startsWith("/");` L109-110: denies only when `namedHosts(command).filter((h) => !isLocal(h))` is non-empty. guardrails.mdc L11: "The project's hook blocks these commands." Cloud SQL Auth Proxy Unix sockets live under /cloudsql/INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME (https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/connect-auth-proxy, not fetched).
findings.suggested_fix: Allow only an explicit list of local socket paths. Deny a Postgres client when it has no explicit local host, or when it uses a $VAR, a service= value or a URI built from variables. Change the rule text to say the hook is a backstop, not a guarantee.

findings.claim: Only beforeShellExecution is hooked. A database or cloud-provider MCP server, or a script run through a language runtime (for example `python -c` with psycopg, or `aws rds-data execute-statement`), can reach production without hitting any rule. The RDS rule also doesn't cover rds-data, stop or start, or snapshot deletion, and IaC coverage stops at Terraform, OpenTofu and Terragrunt, so `pulumi up` and `cdk deploy` are not blocked.
findings.evidence: hooks.json L4: `"beforeShellExecution": [` (no MCP hook). block-prod-db.mjs L24: PG_CLIENTS lists only CLI binaries. L36: the RDS rule covers `modify|delete|restore|reboot|failover|upgrade` only. L45: `(?:terraform|tofu|terragrunt)`. Cursor hooks also support beforeMCPExecution (https://cursor.com/docs/hooks, not fetched).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a beforeMCPExecution hook that denies database and provider MCP tools, and extend the deny rules to rds-data, AlloyDB, Pulumi, CDK and CloudFormation deploys, and `git push` to default branches.

findings.claim: The rollup decides a Needs approval row is stale from `Last checked`, but the daily status run refreshes `Last checked` on every row it verifies. As a result, "Needs approval for two days or more" is always empty, and owners are never chased.
findings.evidence: tracker-lib.mjs L142: `stale: r.Status === "Needs approval" && r["Last checked"] ? daysBetween(r["Last checked"], today) >= staleDays : false`. tracker SKILL L19: "Set `Last checked` to today on every row you touched or verified." tracker-schema L27: "Last checked ... Set by the daily status run".
findings.suggested_fix: Add a column recording when the row entered its current status (for example `Status since`), and compute staleness from that instead of `Last checked`.

findings.claim: With an external backend, every write starts by exporting the backend's rows over upgrade/tracker.csv. That file is also where earlier failed writes are parked as "pending sync", so the next run can overwrite and lose those updates, which contradicts "never drops updates". The schema and the skill also disagree on how the fallback is marked.
findings.evidence: tracker L49: "Before writing, export the current rows to `upgrade/tracker.csv`". L50: "Write it to `upgrade/tracker.csv`, add `backend unavailable, pending sync` to that row's `Notes`... Sync the pending rows on the next run." tracker-schema L73: "marks the fallback in `Notes` on the first row it touches ... It never drops updates."
findings.suggested_fix: Keep pending updates in a separate file such as upgrade/tracker-pending.csv, sync and merge them before any export, and use one marking rule in both the schema and the skill.

findings.claim: Catch-up runs bootstrap steps 1 to 3, then says to "skip its repo search until after step 7". The repo search is bootstrap step 4, which isn't part of steps 1 to 3, and step 8 stops before any new work. It is unclear whether the search runs at all, and if it does, bootstrap's approval stop for the repo list (step 6) is bypassed.
findings.evidence: catch-up L12: "run `pg-upgrade-bootstrap` steps 1 to 3 with the handoff's values, then continue here. Skip its repo search until after step 7 below." L23: "Ask the program owner to confirm the summary before you start any new work." bootstrap L31: "Don't continue until a named person approves."
findings.suggested_fix: State plainly that catch-up doesn't run the repo search, and that it lists running bootstrap steps 4 to 6, including the repo-list approval, as a next action after confirmation.

findings.claim: Script paths are relative to the skill folder, but the same command passes `upgrade/tracker.csv`, which is relative to the workspace root. The command can't work from either directory. A plugin install also puts `../../scripts` under the plugin cache, not under the workspace.
findings.evidence: bootstrap L25: "Run `node ../../scripts/tracker-check.mjs upgrade/tracker.csv`" (the same pattern appears in precheck L40, catch-up L22 and tracker L20). workspace-layout.mdc L23: "The plugin's own files are found relative to each skill: ... `../../scripts/`". tracker-check.mjs and render-dashboard.mjs aren't in the review set's scripts/ folder, which holds only tracker-lib.mjs.
findings.suggested_fix: Tell the agent to resolve the skill's absolute directory first and run `node <skill-dir>/../../scripts/tracker-check.mjs <workspace>/upgrade/tracker.csv`. Add a fallback that reports the problem if the script isn't found.

findings.claim: Several references point outside the plugin, or to files that aren't shipped in the folder they name. "The template's" docs/automations.md and docs/catch-up-handoff-template.md live outside plugins/pg-major-upgrade, so they won't be present after a plugin install. Model review points to agents/findings.schema.json, but agents/ contains only the two agent prompts.
findings.evidence: bootstrap L35: "from the template's `docs/automations.md`". catch-up L8: "in the template's `docs/catch-up-handoff-template.md`" (that file isn't in review/docs/). model-review L8: "`../../agents/findings.schema.json`", while review/plugins/pg-major-upgrade/agents/ holds only independent-reviewer.md and sop-auditor.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the automations doc, the handoff template and the findings schema inside the plugin (for example into assets/ and agents/), and add a validation step that checks every relative reference resolves.

findings.claim: After approval, bootstrap starts "one read-only readiness scan per approved repo", but no skill or prompt defines what a scan checks, what it returns, or which tracker columns it fills. Different models will produce scans that don't line up, and the Consumer columns gate G0.1 relies on (Auth, Driver and version, CDC, Hazards) will be filled inconsistently.
findings.evidence: bootstrap L33: "Start one read-only readiness scan per approved repo, up to `concurrency` at a time, and link each in `Session or PR`." No readiness-scan skill or prompt exists under skills/.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a readiness-scan prompt or skill that lists the checks (driver version, auth method, hard-coded hosts, CDC config, removed settings in IaC), the Consumer columns to fill, and whether the scan may open draft PRs.

findings.claim: project.json fields are named but have no defined types or formats. `window` has to cover minutes, read/write versus write-only, and timing, while the runbook computes 75% of it; programOwners and orgs could be strings or arrays. Two models will write incompatible files for render-dashboard and the runbook math.
findings.evidence: bootstrap L17: "Use the fields `name`, ..., `window`, `rpo`, ... `programOwners`, ... `orgs`" (no types). bootstrap-prompt.md: "Downtime window: {{minutes}}, {{read/write or write-only}}, {{when, e.g. weekend night}}". runbook L32: "compare the total with 75% of the window (G2.1)".
findings.suggested_fix: Ship a JSON schema for project.json, with `window` as an object such as `{minutes, mode, when}`, arrays for owners, orgs and reviewers, ISO dates, and `"unknown"` handling defined for each type.

findings.claim: The latest rollback decision time is computed as the window end minus the rehearsed restore time. That leaves no margin for variance, even though the skill flags a 25% overrun on other steps, and it ignores rollback steps outside the restore, such as rerouting connections and rebuilding replicas. A rollback started at that moment will likely overrun the window.
findings.evidence: runbook L33: "Compute the latest rollback decision time as the window end minus the restore time." L40: "Flag any step running past its rehearsed time plus 25%". The provider's rollback goes through a new recovery instance, which needs rerouting: S-01 quote "recovery instance, which is a new instance running the pre-upgrade version".
findings.suggested_fix: Define the latest decision time as window end minus (rehearsed end-to-end rollback time, including rerouting and validation, × 1.25), and require the go or no-go owner to approve that number in the runbook.

findings.claim: The provider precheck request and the reading guide cover only Cloud SQL, yet the plugin's hook covers RDS and Azure too. On another provider, the part-1 check "Provider outputs present" can never pass, and the skill gives no instruction, so the agent either guesses at commands or blocks G0.2 for good.
findings.evidence: precheck L16: "On Cloud SQL that's `gcloud sql instances pre-check-major-version-upgrade`" (no other provider). reading guide L17: "Provider outputs present | Precheck JSON, `operations describe` JSON, `instances describe` YAML". block-prod-db.mjs L36 and L40 have RDS and Azure rules.
findings.suggested_fix: Either limit the plugin's scope to Cloud SQL in the descriptions, or add a provider table, and when the provider isn't supported, add a Question row and stop instead of improvising.

findings.claim: When a reviewer fails, the skill says to continue with the others, but sets no minimum. A gate can be signed off after a "multi-model" review where only one reviewer, or none, actually ran.
findings.evidence: model-review L34: "A reviewer that fails leaves a `.err` file. Report it, and continue with the others." L12: "Use three or four reviewers from different model families."
findings.suggested_fix: Require at least two successful reviewers from different families. Below that, mark the review incomplete and tell the gate owner that the gate can't use it.

findings.claim: The skill sends project artifacts, including customer names, instance names and risks, to external model vendors through the Codex CLI. It never checks the project's `compliance` field or whether those vendors are approved. For regulated customers, that may breach their data-handling terms.
findings.evidence: model-review L21: "`codex:<model>`: `../../scripts/review-with-codex.sh`. It needs the Codex CLI installed and signed in." bootstrap L17 records `compliance` but nothing reads it. bootstrap-prompt.md: "Compliance: {{e.g. regulated data; ...}}".
findings.suggested_fix: Before running the round, read `compliance` from project.json, and use only backends the program owner has approved for this customer, listed in a field such as `approvedReviewBackends`.

findings.claim: The tracker-update step says what to do for pass and fail but not for `needs decision`. The schema also lets a block exit with Waived gates, while gate review lets a block exit only on pass, so the two disagree about waived gates.
findings.evidence: gate-review L29-30 cover only `pass` (Needs approval) and `fail` (Blocked). L23: "A block exits only when every gate in it is `pass`". tracker-schema L54: "A block has exited only when every gate in it is `Done` or `Waived`."
findings.suggested_fix: Map `needs decision` to Needs approval, with the missing sign-off named in Notes, and say how a Waived gate counts toward block exit in both files.

findings.claim: Bootstrap's fallback adds a fixed ID, Q-07, while the step before it says new question rows start at Q-20, and the tracker skill says to use the next free ID and never reuse one. The precheck skill's reference to "question Q-08" suggests the seed already has Q-0x rows, so Q-07 may collide with an existing row.
findings.evidence: bootstrap L18: "add a `Question` row (ID `Q-20` and up)". L24: "Add question row `Q-07` asking for the repo list". tracker L17: "New rows get the next free ID for their prefix. Never reuse an ID." precheck L17: "for question Q-08".
findings.suggested_fix: Say whether Q-07 is a seed row to update or a new row to add. If it's new, use the next free ID.

findings.claim: The consumer search looks for connection strings, and its results are shown in chat and recorded as evidence. Nothing says to redact credentials found in hits, so passwords embedded in URIs can end up in chat, the tracker or Slack.
findings.evidence: bootstrap L19: "Search ... connection strings, hostnames, ... env var names". L28: "The repo list with its evidence". tracker L57: "Don't put row data, query text or secrets in any cell."
findings.suggested_fix: Record only the file path and line, never the matched text. Add a Finding row for any hard-coded credential, with the value redacted.

findings.claim: B0-03 and B0-04 are set to Waiting on customer as soon as the request is drafted, before anyone sends it. The tracker then shows the customer as the blocker when the request may never have gone out.
findings.evidence: precheck L20: "Save the draft ... and set B0-03 and B0-04 to `Waiting on customer`. A person sends it; you don't."
findings.suggested_fix: Set the rows to In progress, with "request drafted, not sent" in Notes, and move them to Waiting on customer only when a person confirms they sent it.

findings.claim: The schema tells users to set `tracker_backend`, but project.json and the tracker skill read `trackerBackend`, and the bootstrap prompt's field is just "Tracker:". With the wrong key, the project silently falls back to CSV.
findings.evidence: tracker-schema L63: "set `tracker_backend` in the bootstrap prompt". tracker SKILL L8: "unless `upgrade/project.json` sets `trackerBackend`". bootstrap L17: "`trackerBackend` (default `project`)".
findings.suggested_fix: Use `trackerBackend` everywhere, and have the tracker skill warn when it finds an unrecognized backend key.

findings.claim: The dashboard step copies into a local `~/.cursor/projects/<workspace>/canvases/` path, but never says how to resolve `<workspace>` and has no fallback for cloud agents or Project runs where that path doesn't exist.
findings.evidence: tracker L42: "copy the output into the workspace's canvases folder (`~/.cursor/projects/<workspace>/canvases/pg-upgrade-dashboard.canvas.tsx`)".
findings.suggested_fix: Say how to resolve the folder. If it doesn't exist, leave the file at upgrade/dashboard.canvas.tsx and link that instead.

findings.claim: S-10 has status `changed`, meaning a quote no longer matches the live page, yet the reading guide still cites it as plain fact. S-34 to S-37 have no `status`, `verified` or `lastChecked` fields, so the SOP auditor can't report their verified date or tell whether they are stale.
findings.evidence: sources.json L152: `"status": "changed"` for S-10, which reading guide L58 cites: "Cloud SQL maintenance doesn't update the catalog version [S-10]." S-34 (L616) to S-37 have only id, title, url, supports and quotes. sop-auditor L22: "If the source's `verified` date is more than 30 days old". The live page couldn't be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Recheck S-10 and update its quotes before it is cited, or label the 8f claim Unverified. Run check-sources on S-34 to S-37 so they get status and dates.

findings.claim: The guide cites S-01 for two facts that none of S-01's recorded quotes contain: that generated columns on unlogged tables fail the Cloud SQL upgrade, and that DMS drops UPDATE and DELETE on keyless tables "even with full or index identity" (the second is cited to S-13). The citation rule requires a quote that supports each claim.
findings.evidence: reading guide L44: "`has_generated_columns = t` fails the Cloud SQL upgrade [S-01]." L43: "lose UPDATEs and DELETEs even with `full` or `index` identity [S-13]". The S-01 quote list has nothing about generated columns, and S-13's quote is only "UPDATE and DELETE statements aren't migrated for tables without primary keys". The live pages couldn't be fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the exact supporting sentences to S-01 and S-13 in sources.json after checking the pages, or label both claims Inferred or Unverified.
